newsitem.title: CANADA: Busang announcement may comes this week - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Busang announcement may comes this week - analysts.

text.p: The saga involving the huge Busang gold deposit in Indonesia could come to a head this week, analysts said on Monday.
Last week, the Indonesian government urged Canada's Barrick Gold Corp and Bre-X Minerals Ltd to announce an agreement to develop the Busang find.
So far the companies have held their tongues, but analysts said they expected developments this week.
"The Indonesian government wants to get something done. It may well happen this week," said gold mining analyst Michael Fowler with Levesque Beaubien Geoffrion.

The two companies said in December that they reached a proposed deal to split Busang between themselves and the Indonesian government. But they said they wanted Indonesia's guidance on a few issues and the government's stamp of approval before announcing the deal to shareholders.
Indonesia's mines minister said last week that the government was waiting for the companies to make a public announcement.
"I think it's a bit of a standoff," said Fowler. "Everybody's waiting for each other to make the first move."
Neither company returned calls on Monday.
The Muslim holy month of Ramadan starts next week and business will slow down, adding extra pressure to seal the deal this week, analysts said.

The structure of the deal could be holding up an announcement, they said. "The government wants some sort of indication that it will be acceptable to shareholders" before it acts, said one source close to the situation.

In November, the government asked Bre-X, which controls the 57 million-ounce deposit, to form a joint venture with Barrick, with Bre-X keeping 25 percent, Barrick getting 75 percent and the companies giving the government 10 percent.
Indonesia's PT Askatindo Karya Mineral already has a 10 percent stake in the richest parts of the Busang property.
Askatindo's Canadian partner, Minorca Resources Inc, said on Monday that Askatindo's stake was secure.
"We're completely satisfied that they will have at least their 10 percent interest," said Minorca president Roland Horst.
"We've continued to receive assurances from very high levels that their interest is protected."
